mentions.name: FinBodhi
mentions.description: A local-first browser PWA for personal finance built on double-entry accounting, which lets complicated sets of transactions and accounts be modeled. All financial data stays on the user's system (SQLite over OPFS in the browser); sync data is encrypted with the user's key before leaving the device, and backups can be made locally or to Dropbox. It is designed so the builders cannot access user data. Features include multi-currency support, visualizations, and a sheet for complex calculations such as taxes and future planning. A demo account is available with no sign-in required (not working in Firefox private mode).
mentions.problem: Complicated sets of transactions and accounts are hard to model in personal finance, and users' financial data is typically accessible to the services they use; FinBodhi is designed so its builders cannot access user data.
